DC.DC.Title: NPNF1-10. St. Chrysostom: Homilies on the Gospel of Saint Matthew
DC.DC.Creator: St. Chrysostom

div1.title: Preface to the American Edition.
div1.p: This volume, according to the previous announcement of the publishers, contains a reprint of the Oxford edition of the Homilies of St. Chrysostom on the gospel of St. Matthew. It is a preface and must never become an entry.

div1.title: The Homilies of St. John Chrysostom.

div2.title: Homily 1
div2.p:
It were indeed meet for us not at all to require
[μηδὲ δεῖσθαι, “not even to need,” as below in sec. 2.—R.]the aid of the written Word, but to exhibit a life so pure, that the grace of the Spirit should be instead of books to our souls, and that as these are inscribed with ink, even so should our hearts be with the Spirit. But, since we have utterly put away from us this grace, come, let us at any rate embrace the second best course.

For that the former was better, God hath made manifest, both by His words, and by His doings. Since unto Noah, and unto Abraham, and unto his offspring, and unto Job, and unto Moses too, He discoursed not by writings, but Himself by Himself, finding their mind pure.

div2.title: Matthew I. 1.
div2.p: “The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the Son of David, the Son of Abraham.”

Do ye indeed remember the charge, which we lately made you, entreating you to hearken unto all the things that are said with all silence, and mystical quietness? For
[καὶ γὰρ; but there is some variation in the readings.—R.]we are to-day to set foot within the holy vestibule, wherefore I have also put you in mind of the charge.

2. But what is this vestibule? “The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, Son of David, Son of Abraham.” Stay, seek not to learn all at once, but gently and by little and little, for it is in the vestibule that thou art standing, by the very porch, as the Prophet Esaias hath told thee.

div2.title: Matthew I. 1.
div2.p: Behold a third discourse on the same first verse of the genealogy, which the preacher takes up again because his hearers asked for the difficulties to be resolved one by one, and this discourse runs on until the seventeenth verse begins the next.

div2.title: Matthew I. 17.
div2.p: The fourth homily begins at the seventeenth verse, where the evangelist sums the generations into three parts of fourteen, and the preacher asks wherefore he hath not in the third division maintained the number, which question he had raised in the first discourse.

div2.title: Matthew II. 1, 2.
div2.p: The fifth homily has no scripCom element at all, as none in the thirteenth volume do, and its passage is known only from the title of the division: the second chapter, verses one and two, where the wise men come from the east to Jerusalem.
